title: Rabbi Elazar Bei R”Sh
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 8:3 mentions him reporting Rav Hoshaya; Hyman finds no other mention of him. Since the name is abbreviated, Hyman considers “son of R' Shmuel” or “son of Rabbi Shimon” possible readings. It seems more likely to Hyman, however, that Rabbi Elazar spoke to R' Shmuel—that is, Shmuel, Rav’s colleague—in R' Hoshaya’s name.

notes.text: Bei R”Sh may indicate Shmuel or Shimon as a father; Hyman instead proposes Elazar addressing Shmuel. These represent different relationships, so the abbreviated heading is not resolved to one of them.

The saved whole Venice Eruvin 8:3 scalar explicitly reads full Rabbi Elazar bei Rabbi Shimon in Rav Hoshaya's name. This supports one concrete patronymic alternative, without deciding the heading's abbreviation in Hyman's own edition. Hyman's Shmuel-as-father and Elazar-addressing-Shmuel proposals give different relationships; the latter is not a spelling expansion. His MORE LIKELY judgment is retained at that force. במ״א means elsewhere, not specifically the Mishnah and other sources. Supplied full Rav Hoshaya remains distinct from the later abbreviated R' Hoshaya in Hyman's reconstruction; Shmuel's hypothesized title is not established by the Shimon witness.

Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 8:3 in the Venice and Guggenheimer Hebrew witnesses names Rabbi Elazar bei Rabbi Shimon transmitting in Rav Hoshaya’s name. Rashba, in the digital edition at Eruvin 85b, quotes the same ruling as Rabbi Elazar in Rav Hoshaya’s name and omits the patronymic. The parallel in the Bavli is attributed to Rav. Hyman’s preferred reading, in which Rabbi Elazar speaks to Shmuel, remains his proposal.
